title: Summit and Current
premise: Ada Montrose, a storm chaser hiding from creditors in the river town of Kessel's Landing, is dragged into a rescue when an upriver survey expedition—including her estranged brother Theo—goes silent. The expedition's financier, a charismatic optimist named Corvin Hale, bankrolls her crossing but wants the expedition's mineral survey destroyed or delivered, whichever serves him. As Ada and a ragtag crew cross the range ahead of the snows, she learns the expedition didn't die of weather: they found something worth killing for, and Theo chose survival over his crew. In the end, Ada reaches the pass with the truth instead of the survey, lets the mountains keep the ore's location, and chooses her found crew over the debt that bought them—paying Hale back with evidence that ruins him rather than enriches either of them.
about_author: Jonah Blackwood is a former river guide who spent six seasons in remote northern waters before turning to writing. He lives off-grid half the year and claims his best plots come from other people's bad decisions.

chapters.title: The Debt of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Kessel's Landing, dry season's last weeks: Ada dodges creditors and chases storms for hire until Corvin Hale arrives with money and a missing-expedition problem—her brother Theo among the lost. She refuses, then finds her boat burned as leverage. Emotional beat: resentment curdling into reluctant obligation; Ada realizes invisibility was always someone else's permission.

chapters.title: Upriver Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and crew POV. Ada assembles a mismatched team—radio tech Sefa, disgraced guide Bram—and follows the expedition's abandoned camps upstream, finding signs of orderly departure and one violent end. A storm forces them to shelter with a river family who feed them and warn them back. Emotional beat: the fragile first stitches of found family forming under shared fear.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Kept
chapters.summary: Bram's POV at the high camp. They find the expedition alive but broken—Theo among survivors who mutinied against their own leader over a rich ore strike Hale demanded be kept secret. When Hale's second team arrives armed, the camp fractures; Theo confesses he traded his crew's safety for passage out. Climax: a blizzard assault on the pass, Sefa lost saving the radio, Ada choosing to carry people instead of data.

chapters.title: Current
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Downriver ahead of the snows, Ada delivers not the survey but testimony—the survivors' accounts—to the town and the company's rivals, letting the mountain keep its secret. Hale's credit collapses; her debt dies with it. Theo leaves to make amends; Ada stays with Sefa and Bram, rebuilding the burned boat into a home. Emotional beat: survival's price paid honestly, belonging chosen rather than owed.
